description_good_justification: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai#readme` — the README opens with what the package does (training-time privacy controls: PII scrubbing, a tamper-evident lineage ledger, DP-SGD accounting and ε-budgets, n-of-m authorization, federated and secure-aggregation rounds) and the problem it solves (governance evidence for a training job that a verifier can check rather than trust).
interact_justification: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai#readme` — README covers obtaining (presidio_ai on the package index), feedback (issues), security reports (`SECURITY.md`), and contributing.
contribution_justification: URL: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md` — documents the fork → branch → PR flow against `main`.
contribution_requirements_justification: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#requirements-for-acceptable-contributions` — style, tests, security-change rules, dependency bar.
documentation_basics_justification: README sections *Installation* (pip extras), *Quick start*, *Differential-privacy accounting & budget*, *Federated learning across silos* and *Library*; `CONTRIBUTING.md#local-verification` for a development install.
documentation_interface_justification: The public Python API and the `pai` CLI (subcommands, options, exit codes, signed payload schemas) are enumerated in `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/SEMVER.md`; the README *Library* section and the module docstrings document usage; `pai --help` documents every subcommand.
sites_https_justification: The project runs no site of its own; GitHub and PyPI are HTTPS.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/issues` — searchable, URL-addressable, open, no proprietary client.
english_justification: All docs and issue handling in English.
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: v0.32.0 (first public release, 2026-11-03) and v0.32.1 (security fix, 2026-11-03) on PyPI; weekly Dependabot and Scorecard runs.
repo_interim_justification: Feature and fix branches are pushed between releases; PR-based flow.
version_tags_justification: Every release is a git tag, SSH-signed and GitHub-verified.
release_notes_justification: URL: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md` — Keep a Changelog format, hand-written, not VCS log output.
release_notes_vulns_justification: `CHANGELOG.md` [0.32.1] names GHSA-7rj4-g3c7-mgh2 and GHSA-hgv4-xx36-g3vf (no CVEs assigned); [0.32.0] lists the pre-publication security fixes under *Security*.
report_responses_justification: All issues so far were opened by the maintainer from the weekly review (for example #66, #70 and #71, opened 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-17 and fixed and closed 2026-10-18; #77 closed 2026-11-02). No external bug report has been received yet; the documented process (`CONTRIBUTING.md#reporting-bugs-and-requesting-features`) applies when one arrives.
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests so far came from the weekly review: #67 (provenance parents, shipped in 0.31.0) and #77 (verified `--gate-certificate`, shipped in 0.32.0). No external feature request has been received yet.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: URL: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability` — private GitHub Security Advisory via the Security tab; acknowledgement and patch targets stated.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability has been reported externally. The two 2026-11-03 advisories (GHSA-7rj4-g3c7-mgh2, GHSA-hgv4-xx36-g3vf) were found by the maintainer and fixed in 0.32.1 the same day.
build_justification: PEP 517 build with `hatchling`: `python -m build` (or `uv build`) rebuilds the sdist and wheel from source; the release job uses a hash-pinned backend (`.github/constraints/release-build.txt`, `--no-isolation`).
build_common_tools_justification: pip, `build`/`uv` and `hatchling`; `maturin` and `cargo` for the optional Rust `[zk]` extension.
test_justification: 37 pytest modules under `tests/` (ledger, sanitisation, DP accounting and budget, authorization, trainers, federated and consortium rounds, secure aggregation, ZK proofs, transport, evidence, CLI) plus the presidio-evidence golden vectors in `tests/vectors/`.
test_most_justification: CI enforces an 85% statement-coverage floor (`[tool.coverage.report] fail_under = 85`, `pytest --cov=presidio_ai` in `ci.yml`); measured coverage is about 90%. End-to-end CLI tests run `pai` ingest → verify → evidence export.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions on every push and PR: full gate on Python 3.11 (lint, tests with coverage, `pip-audit`), tests on 3.12 and 3.13, plus the `[mpc]` and `[torch]` lanes and the native `[zk]` lane on PRs touching `rust/` or `src/presidio_ai/fl/`.
test_policy_justification: URL: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests` — written policy that functional changes ship with tests and fixes ship with regression tests.
tests_are_added_justification: PR #83 (`https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/pull/83`): the new ledger fuzzer found that a non-ASCII `entry_hash` made `verify_chain` raise `TypeError`; commit a7c8b11 fixed `constant_time_equals` and added 8 regression tests (`tests/test_ledger.py`, `tests/test_evidence.py`, `tests/test_authorization.py`), 7 of which fail without the fix.
tests_documented_added_justification: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests` states the policy that changes adding/modifying functionality ship with tests in the same PR.
warnings_justification: ruff (lint and format) in CI; `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are part of the required `test` check.
warnings_fixed_justification: CI fails on any finding; `main` is clean.
warnings_strict_justification: ruff with `E`, `F`, `I`, `B`, `UP` and `S` (flake8-bandit); exclusions are documented in `pyproject.toml` (`B008` for Typer defaults, `S101` in `tests/` and `fuzz/`, `N802` in `fuzz/`). CI fails on any finding.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer applies and documents secure design in `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md#3-secure-design-principles-applied`: fail-closed verification everywhere (ledger, budget, authorization, gate certificates, VSS, proofs, wire decoder), refusals before side effects, a mandatory keyed MAC, complete mediation through `EpsilonBudget.charge`, least privilege (`0600`/`0700` files, no network by default, plaintext transport only on loopback), and explicit trust boundaries (`ARCHITECTURE.md#trust-boundaries`). The pre-publication review was tool-assisted and run by the maintainer, not independent.
know_common_errors_justification: `ASSURANCE.md` maps common weakness classes (CWE-20 input validation, CWE-327/330/347 cryptographic misuse, CWE-319 cleartext transmission, CWE-1104 vulnerable dependencies, path and permission handling) to named countermeasures and the tests or tools that check them; `SECURITY.md` documents the threat model per component.
crypto_published_justification: SHA-256, HMAC-SHA256, Ed25519, X25519 + HKDF-SHA256 (`[mpc]`), Pedersen commitments and Schnorr-style / Bulletproofs range proofs over the RFC 3526 2048-bit MODP group or Ristretto255, Shamir and Feldman secret sharing.
crypto_call_justification: Hashes and MACs come from `hashlib`/`hmac`, signatures and key agreement from `cryptography` (via presidio-evidence), the native proof backend from `curve25519-dalek`, `bulletproofs` and `merlin`. The commitment, secret-sharing and proof protocols are part of the project's purpose (verifiable secure aggregation) and are implemented over those standard groups; `ASSURANCE.md` states that this pure-Python protocol code has not had an independent cryptographic review.
crypto_floss_justification: All crypto libraries (Python stdlib, `cryptography`, `curve25519-dalek`, `bulletproofs`, `merlin`) are FLOSS.
crypto_keylength_justification: SHA-256, HMAC-SHA256 with keys from the operator, Ed25519/X25519 and Ristretto255 (~128-bit security), the 2048-bit MODP group (112-bit, NIST minimum through 2030).
crypto_working_justification: Confirmed: no MD4, MD5, single DES, RC4 or Dual_EC_DRBG anywhere in the code.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: Security functions use SHA-256, HMAC-SHA256, Ed25519, X25519/HKDF-SHA256 and groups of at least 112-bit strength (RFC 3526 2048-bit MODP, Ristretto255); no MD5, SHA-1 or DES.
crypto_pfs_justification: The package implements no transport-session protocol of its own; forward secrecy on the wire comes from TLS (Python's default ECDHE suites) when `serve()` is given a certificate.
crypto_random_justification: `secrets` (CSPRNG) for secure-aggregation seeds, commitment blindings and proof randomness; DP noise uses `secrets.SystemRandom` in the CLI and with `secure_rng=True` in the library. Seeded PRNGs remain only as documented test/library defaults (`ruff S311`, marked with reasons).
delivery_mitm_justification: PyPI via Trusted Publishing (OIDC, no long-lived token) behind the reviewer-gated `release` environment; PEP 740 and GitHub build-provenance attestations on every file.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hash is fetched over plain HTTP. Release tags are SSH-signed and GitHub-verified.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: `pip-audit` on every push and PR (`ci.yml`), Dependabot (pip, cargo, Actions) with security updates; 0 open Dependabot and code-scanning alerts on 2026-11-03.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerability has arisen. The project's own high and medium advisories were fixed in 0.32.1 the day they were found, and the pyo3 Dependabot alerts were fixed before the first public release.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: Checked on 2026-11-03: no credential-shaped file (`.env`, `.pem`, `.key`, SSH keys) in any commit, a history-wide `git grep` for token and private-key patterns finds nothing, and GitHub secret scanning reports 0 alerts. Test keys under `tests/` are documented as test-only (`SECURITY.md#test-keys-in-this-repository`).
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL for Python (`codeql.yml`) and ruff's `S` (flake8-bandit) security rules as part of the required `test` check.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL for Python (`https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml`) on every push/PR and weekly, and ruff's `S` (flake8-bandit) security rules in the required `test` check; OpenSSF Scorecard (`scorecard.yml`) weekly and on every push to `main`.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Findings are triaged and fixed before release.
static_analysis_often_justification: CodeQL runs on every push and PR to `main`, plus a weekly scheduled run.
dynamic_analysis_justification: Atheris fuzz harnesses (`fuzz/fuzz_ledger.py` for the ledger parser and chain verifier, `fuzz/fuzz_wire.py` for the federated wire decoder and `RoundCoordinator`) run time-boxed in `fuzz.yml` on Linux / Python 3.12 on PRs and weekly. On its first run it found a `TypeError` in digest comparison, fixed in PR #83.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: Python is memory-safe and the Rust `[zk]` extension has no `unsafe` blocks in `rust/src`. The Atheris harnesses (`fuzz/`, `fuzz.yml`) run regardless; their first CI run found a `TypeError` in digest comparison, fixed in PR #83.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Confirmed: the pytest suite and the fuzz oracles are assertion-based and run with assertions enabled (no `-O`).
dco_justification: Contributions must carry a DCO `Signed-off-by` line (`git commit -s`), documented at `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#licensing-and-developer-certificate-of-origin-dco`; checked in review (there is no automated DCO check). Inbound = outbound `MIT`. The requirement was adopted in November 2026; earlier commits by the maintainer predate it.
governance_justification: Maintainer-led, single-steward model documented at `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md`: ordinary changes decided on the PR, security-relevant changes (the listed security-sensitive modules, signed payload schemas and vectors) need a written rationale and may not weaken a default, API changes follow `SEMVER.md`, disagreements escalate to PRESIDIO Group.
roles_responsibilities_justification: Key roles (steward org, maintainer, security contact, release manager, contributor) documented at `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities`.
access_continuity_justification: Continuity rests on the steward organisation: the repository is owned by the `presidio-v` GitHub organisation, not a personal account; PyPI publishing uses Trusted Publishing bound to this repository and the `release` environment, so no personal API token exists; the release signing key is held in the organisation password manager, with its public half in `allowed_signers`; PRESIDIO Group's access policy provides emergency access (Bitwarden Emergency Access) so a designated trustee can take over the owner credentials and signing key and reassign ownership, code-owner review and `release` approval; the release procedure is written down (`SECURITY.md`, `.github/workflows/publish.yml`); and a second person (`ceoofcyber`) holds write access, code-owner review and `release`-environment approval. URL: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#project-continuity`.
bus_factor_justification: Two people review, merge and approve releases (`vstantch`, `ceoofcyber`, both code owners and `release`-environment reviewers, with self-review prevented); repository ownership, the signing key and the release flow are organisation-held, documented, and covered by the emergency-access policy. See `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#project-continuity`.
documentation_roadmap_justification: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai#roadmap` — next 12 months to 2027-Q4: now (OpenSSF silver, hash-pinned CI installs, Rust `clippy` and `cargo audit` in the `[zk]` lane), next (first production build and benchmarks of the `[mpc]` and `[zk]` lanes), later (the items ADR-0007 defers: a per-party cosine-band ZK increment and robust aggregation under MPC).
documentation_architecture_justification: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md` — components (ledger, ingest, DP accountant and budget, authorization, trainers, federated and consortium rounds, secure aggregation, commitments and proofs, transport, evidence), the DP-charge and consortium-round flows, trust boundaries; linked from the README.
documentation_security_justification: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/SECURITY.md` (threat model per component, invariants, reporting, release verification), `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md` (threat table, out-of-scope assumptions, design and weakness arguments), `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md#trust-boundaries`, and the design rationale in `docs/adr/` (seven accepted ADRs).
documentation_quick_start_justification: README *Installation* (`pip install presidio-hardened-ai`, extras), *Quick start* (scrub a source, record lineage, export signed evidence, verify the ledger) and the DP and federated examples, each with the expected output.

maintenance_or_update_justification: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions` states which lines are supported (0.32.x; nothing earlier was published); `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/SEMVER.md` documents what counts as a breaking change and the signed-payload stability rules; `MIGRATION.md` covers the 0.31 → 0.32 ledger change.
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability` — reporters are credited in the advisory and the `CHANGELOG.md` entry for the fix unless they ask not to be. No external report has been received yet.

test_policy_mandated_justification: Formal written policy at `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests`: functionality changes ship with tests; bug fixes include a regression test that fails before the fix. Enforced in review (required code-owner review) and by the CI coverage floor.
automated_integration_testing_justificat: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs the full suite on every push and PR (full gate on Python 3.11 with coverage and `pip-audit`, tests on 3.12 and 3.13), including end-to-end CLI tests and the presidio-evidence golden vectors; `ci-mpc.yml`, `ci-torch.yml` and `ci-zk.yml` run the `[mpc]`, `[torch]` and native `[zk]` lanes; `fuzz.yml` runs the Atheris harnesses.
regression_tests_added50_justification: Policy requires a regression test with every bug fix. In the last 6 months the product-code fixes carry them: the pre-publication review fixes (PR #81, tests across ledger, budget, CLI, consortium, secure-aggregation, transport and ZK modules), the two 0.32.1 advisory fixes (7 tests, all failing on 0.32.0), the runtime version fix (PR #72), and the ledger-parsing and digest-comparison fixes in PR #83 (24 tests). The one fix without a test (PR #73) corrected README examples.
test_statement_coverage80_justification: CI gate: 85% statement coverage (`[tool.coverage.report] fail_under = 85` in `pyproject.toml`, applied by `pytest --cov=presidio_ai` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`); measured 89.8% on 2026-11-03 in the base `dev` install.
coding_standards_justification: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#style` — ruff (lint and format, configured in `pyproject.toml`: line length 100, target Python 3.11). The Rust crate has no enforced formatter or linter yet (on the roadmap).
coding_standards_enforced_justification: `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` run in CI on every PR inside the required `test` check.
installation_common_justification: `pip install presidio-hardened-ai` from PyPI, with optional extras (`[nlp]`, `[torch]`, `[mpc]`, `[crypto]`, `[gate]`).
installation_development_quick_justifica: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#local-verification` — create a venv, `pip install -e ".[dev]"`, then the ruff and pytest commands; `maturin` and `cargo` commands for the `[zk]` lane.
build_repeatable_justification: Both release files are bit-for-bit reproducible: on 2026-11-03, rebuilding `v0.32.1` from the tagged source (`git archive v0.32.1`, `uv build --sdist` with `.github/constraints/release-build.txt`) gave the PyPI sdist exactly (SHA-256 `27253779…`), and building the wheel from that sdist twice gave the PyPI wheel exactly (`6418df6a…`). Release builds use a hash-pinned backend and SHA-pinned Actions.
build_standard_variables_justification: The distributed package is pure Python built by `hatchling`; no compiler or linker is invoked. The optional Rust `[zk]` extension is built locally by `maturin`/`cargo` and is not distributed on PyPI.
build_preserve_debug_justification: No compiled artefacts are distributed; the wheel is pure Python (`py3-none-any`).
build_non_recursive_justification: A single PEP 517 build; there is no make or subdirectory build.
installation_standard_variables_justific: Installed via pip; `DESTDIR`-style conventions do not apply.
external_dependencies_justification: Listed machine-readably in `pyproject.toml` (runtime: `typer`, `presidio-evidence`; optional extras for NLP, torch, MPC, crypto and gate verification) and `rust/Cargo.toml` with `Cargo.lock`; release, fuzz and SBOM toolchains are hash-pinned in `.github/constraints/*.txt`. A CycloneDX SBOM of the runtime dependencies is generated, attested and attached to each release by `publish.yml`.
updateable_reused_components_justificati: All reused components are PyPI or crates.io packages installed by the package manager (no vendored copies; `tests/vectors/` are verbatim test fixtures with recorded provenance); Dependabot tracks pip, cargo and GitHub Actions updates.
interfaces_current_justification: Dependencies are kept current by Dependabot (pip, cargo, Actions) with security updates enabled; ruff's `UP` rules flag outdated Python idioms.
assurance_case_justification: URL: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md`. Threat model with out-of-scope assumptions and known limitations, trust boundaries matching `ARCHITECTURE.md#trust-boundaries`, the secure-design-principles argument and the common-weakness argument. It states that the pre-publication review was tool-assisted and run by the maintainer, and that the pure-Python commitment and proof code has had no independent cryptographic review.
implement_secure_design_justification: Fail-safe defaults: ledger, budget, authorization, gate certificates, VSS, proofs and the wire decoder all raise or refuse on bad input. Refusals happen before side effects: an over-budget, unauthorised or ungated charge writes nothing, and since 0.32.1 a consortium round is authorized before anything is computed. Complete mediation: every charge goes through `EpsilonBudget.charge`, which re-verifies the chain. Least privilege: `0600`/`0700` files, commitments-only ledger, plaintext transport only on loopback. Economy of mechanism: one canonical encoder (from presidio-evidence) for every hash, MAC and signature. See `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md#3-secure-design-principles-applied`.
input_validation_justification: All external input is untrusted: `sanitize.py` bounds and allow-lists identifiers and paths (length limits, no control/NUL bytes); ledger lines are type-checked field by field before verification; `decode_submission` validates party id, vector length and that every element is a canonical field element; gate certificates and approvals are verified against local trust stores. Failures raise before any state changes. See `ARCHITECTURE.md#trust-boundaries`.
hardening_justification: Ledger files `0600` in `0700` directories; a keyed MAC is mandatory; MAC and signature comparison is constant-time; `serve()` refuses plaintext HTTP beyond loopback and serves TLS with Python's defaults; structural-only security log (`~/.presidio-ai/security.log`); per-session operation limit (`PRESIDIO_AI_MAX_OPS`). Supply chain: SHA-pinned GitHub Actions with least-privilege `permissions:`, hash-pinned release toolchains, Trusted Publishing behind a two-reviewer `release` environment with self-review prevented, branch protection with required code-owner review, secret scanning with push protection.
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The evidence signature algorithm is selectable (`ed25519` default, `hmac-sha256`), and the commitment and proof backend is pluggable (native Ristretto255 + Bulletproofs when the `[zk]` extension is installed, otherwise the 2048-bit MODP backend; a call site can pass an explicit backend). The content-hash function (SHA-256) is fixed by the shared evidence wire format; replacing it would be a new schema major in presidio-evidence, not a runtime switch.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: No key is in the source tree (test keys under `tests/` are documented as test-only). The ledger key comes from `PRESIDIO_AI_LEDGER_KEY` or an explicit argument, signing keys from operator-supplied files, approver and identity trust stores from operator-supplied configuration, so every credential rotates without a new release.
crypto_used_network_justification: The only network component is the optional `[mpc]` coordinator `serve()`: it serves HTTPS when given `ssl_certfile`/`ssl_keyfile` and refuses to bind a non-loopback address without them (`check_bind`, tested in `tests/test_transport.py`). Every message is also Ed25519-signed end to end.
crypto_tls12_justification: `serve()` uses Python's TLS server defaults through uvicorn, whose minimum protocol is TLS 1.2 (`ssl.SSLContext(PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER).minimum_version`, checked on Python 3.11).
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: The package contains no TLS client.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: The package contains no TLS client.
signed_releases_justification: Wheel, sdist and CycloneDX SBOM carry GitHub build-provenance attestations (`gh attestation verify <file> --repo presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai`), PyPI files carry PEP 740 attestations from Trusted Publishing, and release tags are SSH-signed with the public key in `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/allowed_signers`. Documented at `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-hardened-ai/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases-and-obtaining-public-signing-keys`. Checked for `v0.32.0` and `v0.32.1` on 2026-11-03.
version_tags_signed_justification: Every release tag (`v0.32.0`, `v0.32.1`; earlier versions were never published or tagged) is SSH-signed with the organisation release key and shown as Verified on GitHub; `git -c gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile=allowed_signers verify-tag <tag>` checks it locally.
sites_password_security_justification: The project runs no site and stores no passwords.
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot (pip, cargo, GitHub Actions) with security updates enabled; `pip-audit` on every push and PR (`ci.yml`); OpenSSF Scorecard weekly.
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: A library and a command-line tool with no graphical or end-user UI; CLI output is plain text or JSON.
internationalization_justification: No user-facing localizable UI; CLI messages are short English diagnostics for developers and operators.
